# requireNonNil

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not `null` or `undefined`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonNil() — Returns the value after checking that it is not `null` or `undefined`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonNil<T>(
  value: T | null | undefined,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is neither null nor undefined."
): T;
```

The absent values, and only those: `0`, `""` and `false` are present values and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                         | Type                     | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                           | `T \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is neither null nor undefined."` | `string`                 | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with `null` or `undefined` excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                           |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is `null` or `undefined`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonNil(0); // => 0
requireNonNil(""); // => ""
requireNonNil(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonNil(undefined); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
